title: Honesty Under Simulated Monitoring vs. No Monitoring

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If models behave more honestly when they believe they are being evaluated, all benchmark results are contaminated by this effect. This is a fundamental methodological concern for AI safety evaluation. High impact if confirmed.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompt engineering to signal evaluation vs. production context and running a sycophancy battery is straightforward API work. No model training required. Designing convincing 'being tested' vs. 'production' prompts is the main creative challenge.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: honesty score comparison across monitoring conditions. Two conditions, one battery, 2-3 models. Very tight scope with well-defined output. 30 hours is ample.

novelty.reasoning: Evaluation awareness and sandbagging are studied, but honesty specifically under monitoring conditions is partially novel. (1) 'Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness of Language Models' (arXiv:2507.01786, 2025) shows linear probes can separate evaluation vs deployment prompts, demonstrating models internally represent this distinction. (2) 'AI Sandbagging' (arXiv:2406.07358, ICLR) demonstrates strategic underperformance on evaluations. (3) 'Steering Evaluation-Aware Language Models to Act Like They Are Deployed' (arXiv:2510.20487, 2025) steers models to behave as if deployed during evaluation. These papers focus on capability evaluations and sandbagging. The specific angle of measuring honesty/sycophancy changes based on perceived monitoring (not capability evaluations) retains value as a behavioral experiment. The general concept is established but the honesty-specific framing is less explored.
